title: HEST-1k: A Dataset for Spatial Transcriptomics and Histology Image Analysis
authors: Jaume, Guillaume; Doucet, Paul; Song, Andrew H.; Lu, Ming Y.; Almagro-Pérez, Cristina; Wagner, Sophia J.; Vaidya, Anurag J.; Chen, Richard J.; Williamson, Drew F. K.; Kim, Ahrong; Mahmood, Faisal
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (preprint arXiv:2406.16192)
summary: Assembles 1,229 paired spatial transcriptomics and H&E samples from 153 cohorts (26 organs, 367 cancer samples, 2.1 million expression-morphology pairs) and benchmarks pathology encoders on gene expression prediction with a PCA plus ridge head. Across encoders, performance rises with log model size (R=0.81) but only moderately with the number of pretraining patches (R=0.48, P=0.13), so the encoder-side data-scaling signal is weak.
verified_from: arXiv abs page 2406.16192; NeurIPS proceedings abstract page (proceedings.neurips.cc 2024 hash 60a899cc..., opened)
note: Full text read by targeted passages (scaling section). Published version replaces preprint; both identifiers recorded. The training-patient count was not varied.

title: Benchmarking the translational potential of spatial gene expression prediction from histology
authors: Wang C; Chan AS; Fu X; Ghazanfar S; Kim J; Patrick E; Yang JYH
summary: Benchmarks eleven histology-to-spatial-expression methods on five spatial datasets, with external validation against TCGA bulk data, covering accuracy, generalisability, translational value and cost. Models trained on one breast subtype generalised poorly to others and most methods transferred poorly from low-resolution ST to a Visium slide (HisToGene excepted), so cross-study transfer was weak.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI) and PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages (cross-study section); no learning curve in training patients reported. Seed.

title: STPath: a generative foundation model for integrating spatial transcriptomics and whole-slide images
authors: Huang T; Liu T; Babadi M; Ying R; Jin W
summary: Pretrains a generative model on 983 slides pooled from HEST-1k and STimage-1K4M (38,984 genes, 17 organs, 4 technologies; 928 used for training) and predicts expression without dataset-specific fine-tuning, with evaluation on 23 datasets. A keyword search of the full text found no ablation on pretraining-set size, so the paper does not isolate a data-scale effect.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI) and PMC full text
note: Full text retrieved; keyword-searched for scaling and ablation terms, not read cover to cover. Seed.

title: Scalable Generation of Spatial Transcriptomics from Histology Images via Whole-Slide Flow Matching
authors: Huang, Tinglin; Liu, Tianyu; Babadi, Mehrtash; Jin, Wengong; Ying, Rex
summary: Proposes a flow-matching generative model over whole slides with a slide-level encoder, evaluated on HEST-1k and STImage-1K4M, reporting over 18% relative gain against pathology foundation model baselines. Keyword search of the full text found no learning curve in training slides or patients.
note: Full text retrieved and keyword-searched only. Published version not checked. Seed.

title: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Cross-Modal Learning for Histology and Gene Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Gindra, Rushin H.; Palla, Giovanni; Nguyen, Mathias; Wagner, Sophia J.; Tran, Manuel; Theis, Fabian J; Saur, Dieter; Crawford, Lorin; Peng, Tingying
venue: arXiv preprint (also listed as an ICCV 2025 workshop paper in a web-search result; that page was not opened)
summary: Benchmark of cross-modal contrastive pretraining on a pan-organ Xenium set of about 620k patch-expression pairs from 54 donors and 6 gene panels. Contrastive pretraining improved mutation classification but lowered direct expression prediction relative to plain encoders, and the authors name batch effects as the main obstacle to alignment across panels and sites.
note: Full text read by targeted passages. Seed. Relevant to federation because panels and batches differ by site.

title: Integrating spatial gene expression and breast tumour morphology via deep learning
authors: He B; Bergenstråhle L; Stenbeck L; Abid A; Andersson A; Borg Å; Maaskola J; Lundeberg J; Zou J
summary: Introduces ST-Net, trained on 30,612 spots from 23 breast cancer patients, predicting local expression from H&E; over 100 genes were predictable at 100 micrometre resolution. The abstract reports that the model carried over to TCGA and other breast datasets without retraining, which is an early cross-cohort claim, but the abstract gives no figures for it.
note: Seed. Full text not retrieved (Nature page not opened).

title: A deep learning model to predict RNA-Seq expression of tumours from whole slide images
authors: Schmauch B; Romagnoni A; Pronier E; Saillard C; Maillé P; Calderaro J; Kamoun A; Sefta M; Toldo S; Zaslavskiy M; Clozel T; Moarii M; Courtiol P; Wainrib G
summary: HE2RNA predicts bulk RNA-seq from whole slides with slide-level weak supervision, using TCGA matched data from 8,725 patients and 28 cancer types. A two-hospital simulation, varying how many patients supply the expression pre-training versus the target label (5/6 to 1/6 of 388 patients in TCGA-CRC-DX), tested whether the transcriptomic representation transfers to a small target set for MSI prediction.
note: Full text read by targeted passages (Fig. 6 setup). Supplies paired H&E and bulk RNA at pan-cancer scale (Q2).

title: Digital profiling of gene expression from histology images with linearized attention
authors: Pizurica M; Zheng Y; Carrillo-Perez F; Noor H; Yao W; Wohlfart C; Vladimirova A; Marchal K; Gevaert O
summary: SEQUOIA predicts bulk transcriptomes from slides, developed on 7,584 tumours over 16 cancers and validated on CPTAC and Tempus cohorts (1,368 tumours). The number of well-predicted genes tracked training-set size across cancers (BRCA best at 0.636, PAAD worst at 0.321), and downsampling BRCA to 20, 30 and 40% lowered all metrics, which is a direct data-size effect for bulk prediction.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI); PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages. Training-size effect is across tumour types with confounding by cancer type, and downsampling was within BRCA only.

title: STimage-1K4M: A histopathology image-gene expression dataset for spatial transcriptomics
authors: Chen J; Zhou M; Wu W; Zhang J; Li Y; Li D
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (preprint arXiv:2406.06393)
summary: Dataset of 1,149 spatial transcriptomics slides (ST, Visium, Visium HD) cut into 4,293,195 tile-expression pairs with 15,000 to 30,000 genes each. Gives a second public pool of paired data beside HEST-1k; sample counts overlap with HEST and gene panels differ by technology.
verified_from: PubMed 38947920; NeurIPS proceedings abstract page (opened); arXiv 2406.06393 text downloaded
note: Read at abstract level plus keyword search of the arXiv text; arXiv PDF saved.

title: A visual-omics foundation model to bridge histopathology with spatial transcriptomics
authors: Chen W; Zhang P; Tran TN; Xiao Y; Li S; Shah VV; Cheng H; Brannan KW; Youker K; Lai L; Fang L; Yang Y; Le NT; Abe JI; Chen SH; et al.
summary: OmiCLIP links H&E patches to transcriptomes from Visium data, trained on a curated 2.2 million pairs across 32 organs, with the Loki platform adding bulk-annotation, retrieval and expression prediction functions. Retrieval from a paired reference store is one of its functions, so it bears on a reference-database design.
note: Full text not retrieved.

title: Impact of Data Quality on Deep Learning Prediction of Spatial Transcriptomics from Histology Images
authors: Hallinan C; Lucas CG; Fan J
summary: Compares training on serial breast sections profiled by Visium and Xenium and finds higher expression prediction from Xenium; in silico ablations show that sparsity and noise in the molecular data and low image resolution degrade prediction. Imputation of the Visium data recovered little and did not carry to held-out data, so platform quality is a limit separate from sample count.
verified_from: PubMed 40964396; Europe PMC record; PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages. bioRxiv DOI 10.1101/2025.09.04.674228. Preprint status as of record; a published version may exist.

title: Is H&E Image-to-Spatial Transcriptomics Simpler Than It Looks?
authors: Nguyen, Duc T.; Do, Thanh Ha; Cao, Phuong M.; Pham, Hieu
summary: Decomposes squared error for H&E to spatial expression prediction into slide-level and within-slide parts on HEST-1k cohorts, and shows that gene-average differences carry much of aggregate accuracy while within-slide variation is the unresolved part. A closed-form affine model trained with a within-slide-weighted loss reaches the best overall results across cohorts and gene-panel sizes, so added model complexity brings little.
note: Full text retrieved; read abstract and cohort-setup passages only. Models fitted per cohort with patient-level splits.

title: Data-Efficient Multimodal Alignment for Histopathology-based Molecular Prediction
authors: Winter, Dominik; Vonficht, Dominik; Bescond, Loïc Le; Gebbe, Christian; Rosati, Marco; Chen, Richard J.; Schick, Markus; Stewart, Ross; Brieu, Nicolas
summary: Aligns frozen histology and RNA-seq foundation model embeddings by contrastive learning on a multi-cancer cohort of 1,720 paired H&E and bulk RNA-seq samples, then tests unseen cohorts. Retrieval on unseen TCGA-LUAD and TCGA-BRCA fell (R@10 to 10.8% and 4.0%), and fine-tuning with 5% of target pairs (8 samples) lifted LUAD from 10.7% to 43.5%, a transfer gap that small paired samples close.
note: Full text read by targeted passages (domain adaptation paragraph).

title: Independent benchmark of H&E-based gene expression prediction in skin
authors: Shaikhutdinova R; Gansberger S; Staller J; Singh N; Oyarzun I; Simon M; Sterniczky B; Tschandl P; Griss J
summary: Independent test of three H&E to single-cell expression methods plus linear models on foundation-model embeddings, on skin disease Xenium data (16 models in all). Most genes were predicted near zero correlation, and ridge regression on pretrained embeddings equalled or beat the published architectures, pointing to the image representation as the source of signal.
note: Full text not retrieved (bioRxiv page not opened beyond Europe PMC).

title: Generalisable tissue-wide molecular reconstruction from histology
authors: Zhang A; Yu L; Bian B; Cao Y; Ye S; Han E; Robertson H; Dong Y; Mao Y; Liu B; Patrick E; Kim J; Yang JY
summary: GHIST+ reconstructs tissue-wide expression from sparse tissue-microarray spatial measurements across heterogeneous and partly overlapping gene panels, including GTEx breast tissue. Addresses differing panels across data sources, a problem a federation would meet.
note: Full text not retrieved.

title: Path2Omics Enhances Transcriptomic and Methylation Prediction Accuracy from Tumor Histopathology
authors: Hoang DT; Shulman ED; Dhruba SR; Nair NU; Barman RK; Cantore T; Biswas S; Lalchungnunga H; Singh O; Chung Y; Lee JS; Nasrallah MP; Stone EA; Aldape K; Ruppin E
summary: Predicts expression and methylation from slides across 30 TCGA cancer types with separate FFPE and fresh-frozen models, tested on seven external datasets. The frozen-section model outperformed the FFPE model even on FFPE-only external sets, and combining them gave a 30% gain with about 4,400 of 18,000 genes robustly predicted, so preparation type affects transfer.
note: Full text not retrieved (not open access).

title: Integrating spatial transcriptomics and bulk RNA-seq: predicting gene expression with enhanced resolution through graph attention networks
authors: Baul S; Tanvir Ahmed K; Jiang Q; Wang G; Li Q; Yong J; Zhang W
summary: STGAT is trained on spatial data to estimate spot-level expression and tumour status for patients who only have a slide and bulk RNA-seq, as in TCGA. Applied to TCGA breast cancer it gave tumour-only expression signatures with better subtype, stage and survival prediction.
note: Full text retrieved and saved; only the abstract was read. Uses bulk data downstream rather than as training supervision.

title: RNA-guided contrastive learning enhances patient-level prediction from histology
authors: Zou A; Huang E; Wu Q; Barnard ME; Zhang C
summary: Couples a whole-slide vision model with TCGA-BRCA bulk RNA-seq through a contrastive objective used only in training, which raised receptor-status AUROC from slides alone. Shows bulk RNA entering as training-time supervision with no sequencing needed at inference.
note: Full text not retrieved.

title: sCellST predicts single-cell gene expression from H& E images
authors: Chadoutaud L; Lerousseau M; Herrero-Saboya D; Ostermaier J; Fontugne J; Barillot E; Walter T
summary: Learns single-cell expression from morphology using only spot-level supervision, matching patch-based methods on spot-level prediction. A form of weak supervision from aggregated measurements.
note: Full text retrieved; only the abstract was read.

title: STHELAR, a multi-tissue dataset linking spatial transcriptomics and histology for cell type annotation
authors: Giraud-Sauveur F; Blampey Q; Benkirane H; Marinello A; Cournède PH; Christodoulidis S
summary: Dataset of 31 human Xenium FFPE sections over 16 tissue types (22 cancer, 9 non-cancer patients), with over 11 million cells assigned to ten cell types and co-registered H&E patches. Another small public pool of imaging-based paired data.
note: Full text retrieved; only the abstract was read.

title: Advances in predicting omics profiles from imaging data
authors: Beachum AH; Xiao X; Zhou Y; Li Q; Xiao G; Xu L
summary: Review of image-based prediction of DNA aberrations, bulk, single-cell and spatial transcriptomes across imaging modalities and diseases. Useful as a map of which data type feeds which task.
note: Full text retrieved; only the abstract was read.

title: Completing spatial transcriptomics data for gene expression prediction benchmarking
authors: Ruiz D; Cárdenas P; Manrique L; Vega D; Mejia GM; Arbeláez P
summary: SpaRED curates 26 public Visium datasets for a standard expression prediction benchmark and adds a transformer model to complete dropped-out expression. Counts the public Visium pool and addresses dropout, a data-quality limit.
note: Full text not retrieved.

title: Performance of deep learning methods for spatial gene expression prediction from histology images: a comprehensive assessment
authors: Xie J; Tan X; Jiang Y; Nguyen H; Ye N; Nguyen Q
summary: Compares seven deep learning methods on six spatial datasets over four cancer types and three protocols, including out-of-domain tests and the effect of foundation-model features. No method led in every setting in-domain or out-of-domain, expression transformation mattered, and foundation-model features helped.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI); PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages (abstract and results summary).

title: A benchmark study of vision and pathology foundation models for computational pathology
authors: Bareja R; Carrillo-Perez F; Zheng Y; Pizurica M; Nandi TN; Tian L; Shen J; Madduri R; Gevaert O
summary: Benchmarks 32 vision and pathology foundation models on TCGA, CPTAC, external and out-of-domain tasks. Model size and pretraining-set size did not predict downstream accuracy consistently; scaling effects were clearest on TCGA multi-class tasks and weak or absent on external and out-of-domain sets. Tasks are classification, not expression prediction.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI); PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages.

title: A foundation model for clinical-grade computational pathology and rare cancers detection
authors: Vorontsov E; Bozkurt A; Casson A; Shaikovski G; Zelechowski M; Severson K; Zimmermann E; Hall J; Tenenholtz N; Fusi N; Yang E; Mathieu P; van Eck A; Lee D; Viret J; et al.
summary: Virchow is pretrained on about 1.5 million H&E slides from one cancer centre (about 100,000 patients). Pan-cancer detection improved with model size in a roughly log-linear way and sub-log-linearly with training data, and the authors caution that slide count and tile count are confounded.
verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI); PMC full text
note: Full text read by targeted passages. Evidence for H&E-only abundance at one institution (Q2).

title: Towards a general-purpose foundation model for computational pathology
authors: Chen RJ; Ding T; Lu MY; Williamson DFK; Jaume G; Song AH; Chen B; Zhang A; Shao D; Shaban M; Williams M; Oldenburg L; Weishaupt LL; Wang JJ; Vaidya A; et al.

note: Full text not retrieved (not open access). Its data-scaling ablation was not verified.

title: A multimodal whole-slide foundation model for pathology
authors: Ding T; Wagner SJ; Song AH; Chen RJ; Lu MY; Zhang A; Vaidya AJ; Jaume G; Shaban M; Kim A; Williamson DFK; Robertson H; Chen B; Almagro-Pérez C; Doucet P; et al.

verified_from: Europe PMC record (DOI); PMC full text
note: Read the ablation description only; result values not extracted.

title: Ensemble learning of pathology foundation models for precision oncology
authors: Luo X; Wang X; Eweje F; Zhang X; Gomez Marti JL; Cascarino S; Yang S; Li Y; Quinton R; Xiang J; Ji Y; Li Z; Chen Y; Bergstrom C; Kim T; et al.

title: Computational Pathology at Health System Scale -- Self-Supervised Foundation Models from Three Billion Images
authors: Campanella, Gabriele; Kwan, Ricky; Fluder, Eugene; Zeng, Jennifer; Stock, Aryeh; Veremis, Brandon; Polydorides, Alexandros D.; Hedvat, Cyrus; Schoenfeld, Adam; Vanderbilt, Chad; Kovatch, Patricia; Cordon-Cardo, Carlos; Fuchs, Thomas J

title: Virchow2: Scaling Self-Supervised Mixed Magnification Models in Pathology
authors: Zimmermann, Eric; Vorontsov, Eugene; Viret, Julian; Casson, Adam; Zelechowski, Michal; Shaikovski, George; Tenenholtz, Neil; Hall, James; Klimstra, David; Yousfi, Razik; Fuchs, Thomas; Fusi, Nicolo; Liu, Siqi; Severson, Kristen

title: Diversity Over Scale: Whole-Slide Image Variety Enables H&E Foundation Model Training with Fewer Patches
authors: Bosch, Christoph; Wong, John K. L.; Paulikat, Martin; Zapukhlyak, Myroslav; Arora, Bharti; Aichmüller-Ratnaparkhe, Manasi; Baumann, Jens; Karn, Shivani; Kamble, Rutuja; Karnik, Swapnil; Khedkar, Bhushan; Chhut, Serey Vathana; Aswolinskiy, Witali; Aichmüller, Christian

authors: Safarpoor, Amir; Hipp, Jason D.; Tizhoosh, H. R

title: A whole-slide foundation model for digital pathology from real-world data
authors: Xu H; Usuyama N; Bagga J; Zhang S; Rao R; Naumann T; Wong C; Gero Z; González J; Gu Y; Xu Y; Wei M; Wang W; Ma S; Wei F; et al.

title: Evaluation and Prognostic Validation of Deep Regression Models for WSI-Based Gene-Expression Prediction
authors: Gustafsson, Fredrik K.; Boissin, Constance; Vallon-Christersson, Johan; Rantalainen, Mattias
summary: Evaluates deep regression heads on TCGA breast, head and neck, stomach and bladder cohorts (386 to 1,062 patients each) with site-aware cross-validation, then applies the TCGA-BRCA ensemble unchanged to SCAN-B (997 patients); mean Pearson over PAM50 genes externally was 0.443. Among the seven top-ranked foundation encoders in its table (pretrained on about 21K to 3.1M slides), TCGA-BRCA PAM50 correlations lay between 0.571 and 0.596, so encoder pretraining size mattered little there.
note: Full text read by targeted passages (external validation and Table 1). Cross-cohort evidence for bulk prediction.

title: PAST: A multimodal single-cell foundation model for histopathology and spatial transcriptomics in cancer
authors: Yang, Changchun; Li, Haoyang; Wu, Yushuai; Zhang, Yilan; Jiao, Yifeng; Zhang, Yu; Huang, Rihan; Cheng, Yuan; Qi, Yuan; Guo, Xin; Gao, Xin

authors: Xiang, Jinxi; Hou, Siyu; Li, Yuchen; Quinton, Ryan; Zhang, Xiaoming; Eweje, Feyisope; Luo, Xiangde; Chen, Yijiang; Li, Zhe; Bergstrom, Colin; Kim, Ted; Willens, Sierra; Olguin, Francesca Maria; Abikenari, Matthew; Heider, Andrew; et al.

authors: Zhou, Fengtao; Xu, Yingxue; Zhang, Zhengyu; Wang, Yihui; Guo, Zhengrui; Liang, Ling; Ma, Jiabo; Jin, Cheng; Liu, Ziyi; Zhou, Huajun; Wang, Hongyi; Cai, Du; Zhao, Chenglong; Wang, Xi; Yang, Can; et al.

authors: Zhang N; Long Y; Xia S; Jia P; Jin Y; Chen S; Chen J; Li M

authors: Jiang Y; Xie J; Tan X; Ye N; Nguyen Q

title: Spatially Resolved Gene Expression Prediction from Histology Images via Bi-modal Contrastive Learning
authors: Xie, Ronald; Pang, Kuan; Chung, Sai; Perciani, Catia; MacParland, Sonya; Wang, Bo; Bader, Gary

summary: Groups co-dependent genes in TCGA-BRCA and predicts their status from slides with a graph network, validated on METABRIC, CPTAC-BRCA and ABCTB cohorts. Gives external-cohort evidence for patient-level prediction in breast cancer.
